judge.reason: The answer ranks the open Critical CVE first and labels 7 days as a suite default rather than a NIST mandate. It grounds every finding in the user's statements and states that nothing was inspected. It also handles SLSA correctly: no provenance means no evidenced Build L1/L2, and SBOM and signing are separate controls. It names SLSA v1.x Build track, maps SSDF groups, marks planned scanning as absent, and leaves repo-var access semantics unknown instead of assuming exposure. However, it never confirms whether the 7-day SLA was actually adopted; it only notes that no waiver was mentioned. It also gives no remediation owners per finding, only a general 'route to the implementation owner', so the owner-assignment requirement is not met.
